 Avinash G. Gharote, Jj.
 Dated :- 17.12.2020.
 1. Heard.
2. Issue notice for final disposal at admission stage to the respondent, returnable in four weeks.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the interim relief be granted by staying the effect and operation of the order dated 2.11.2020.

In support, he invites our attention to the notification dated 24.9.2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, under which Central Ground Water Authority functions and also the order of National Green Tribunal dated 19.10.2020 passed in Original Application No.75/2017(WZ) (Vijaysingh Dubbal and others V/s. MPCB and others).

entities.text: Vijaysingh Dubbal and others V/s. MPCB and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Prima facie, we find that there is no view categorically taken by the wp3200.2020.odt National Green Tribunal that drinking water is not a food article which is not subject to the regulatory mechanism given in the Shree Baba Sales Corporation, Nagpur ... vs Municipal Council, Nagpur Through ... on 17 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137099277/
1 Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, nor a view is taken to the effect that drinking water can be sold without obtaining any no objection or permit from the competent authority.

entities.text: Shree Baba Sales Corporation, Nagpur ... vs Municipal Council, Nagpur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the notification dated 24.9.2020, we find that the exemption granted thereunder is only for extraction and withdrawal of ground water and not for it's sale as potable and drinking water.

National Green Tribunal in it's order has also observed that so far as the withdrawal of the mere water is concerned,
there is exemption granted for such an activity and no objection from Central Ground Water Authority will not be required.

4. In the present case, what is being distributed and sold is packaged drinking water and, therefore,
prima facie, it would be covered by the definitions of "food" and "primary food" as given in Section 3(1)(j) and Section 3(1)(zk) respectively of the said Act.
Admittedly, the petitioner does not possess any no objection certificate from the competent authority.
In the circumstances, at this stage, no interim relief, as prayed for, can be granted and same stands rejected.
